_description: Synthetic Azure AD authentication event sequences for DeepLog LSTM training. Follows the methodology of Du et al. (CCS 2017): train on normal sequences; flag deviations at inference. In production, replace with real session logs from Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel, or your SIEM.
_methodology: Normal sequences represent typical enterprise authentication patterns based on Microsoft documentation and Azure AD error code semantics. Anomalous sequences represent known attack patterns (credential stuffing, account takeover) and misconfiguration signatures.

anomalous_sequences.label: credential_stuffing
anomalous_sequences.description: Repeated failed credentials leading to account lockout — classic credential-stuffing signature

anomalous_sequences.label: brute_force
anomalous_sequences.description: 7 consecutive failed credential attempts without lockout — brute force or password spray

anomalous_sequences.label: unusual_transition
anomalous_sequences.description: Disabled account then bad credentials then lockout: unusual ordering

anomalous_sequences.label: account_probing
anomalous_sequences.description: Non-existent user then bad credentials then lockout: account enumeration and stuffing

anomalous_sequences.label: credential_stuffing_then_disable
anomalous_sequences.description: Repeated failed attempts followed by account disable

anomalous_sequences.label: ca_bypass_attempt
anomalous_sequences.description: Repeated conditional access blocks — possible attempt to find CA policy gaps

anomalous_sequences.label: enumeration
anomalous_sequences.description: Alternating bad-creds and not-found errors — systematic account enumeration

anomalous_sequences.label: retry_storm
anomalous_sequences.description: 8+ consecutive transient errors — likely misconfigured retry logic
